stage1.impression: A night view from the kerb through a steel shopfront into a long, warm, timber-ceilinged bar: it is readable and pleasant, but it is lit far too evenly and too brightly for a night room. A milky veil sits over the back half, and the two Ember speakers at the far end are thumbnail-sized salmon rectangles that read as screens or signs, not as an altar. The glass has no reflections, so the 'E' reads as a beige card pasted in the air. At this distance it reads as a generic, nicely furnished restaurant: the record wall and the lightbox hint at a specific place, but a magazine would not run it as one yet.

blocking_9: Frame lum_median at 32-48 with real pools of light and dark between them; at present the room is evenly filled (median 60.1)

The Ember pair has to read at a glance as deep red tinted acrylic cabinets on an altar, not clipped salmon rectangles. Today it shows clip 6-12 % and dE2000 17.5 against red, and the mullion splits the view between them
The shopfront glass has to read as glass: faint street-lamp and kerb reflections across it, an etched name that is translucent and edge-lit rather than an opaque beige panel, and steel with patina
The back third needs contrast; haze is flattening it (p5 48.5 in the altar zone)
The lightbox dancer has to be legible as a figure, and the frame needs a clear reason it is a shopfront shot rather than a doorway view
1:1 craft: concrete floor with formwork/trowel variation and pendant reflections, no denoiser smear on the record spines, and no row of identical stools reading as copies

defects.what: Overall overexposed for a night interior: lum_median 60.1 against a target of 22-50, and 27 % of pixels below 40, so the shadows are thin
Left Ember speaker: clip 6.1 %, lum_p95 208, reads pink-salmon; half hidden behind the centre mullion
Right Ember speaker: clip 12.3 %, r/g/b medians 183/104/93 (salmon, not deep red), dE2000 17.5 against #C8102E; reads as a lit screen or sign
Centre steel mullion splits the frame exactly between the two speakers and through the vanishing point
Record wall is the brightest large surface in the frame (median 106) and pulls the eye away from the altar; the spines are smeared by the denoiser
Banquette wall evenly washed (median 98), with no falloff between the sconces and tables; reads as a showroom
Haze veil over the altar zone: p5 48.5, so no true blacks behind the speakers, and the back looks foggy rather than atmospheric
Etched 'E' on the glass reads as an opaque beige rectangle floating in space, not as etching in glass
Frosted lightbox glows as a flat mauve-grey card (lum_range 94 across it, but no edge glow or falloff); only a cropped fragment of the dancer is visible, so the figure is illegible
Shopfront glass shows no reflection of the street, kerb or street lamps, so there is no evidence the camera is outside behind glass
Floor is a flat brown with no pendant reflections, trowel marks or wear; it reads as CG
Identical stools and bistro tables repeated down the room read as copies of one model
Green objects (lamps or plants) at the back compete with the red speakers for the only saturated colour

changes.problem: The frame is too bright for a night room, so the light pools and the darkness between them are lost.
changes.expected: The whole room drops about two-thirds of a stop; the practicals and pools hold, and the walls and ceiling fall into warm shadow.

changes.problem: The Ember speakers are over-lit from the front, so their red clips to salmon and they read as glowing screens rather than tinted acrylic.

change.setting: on each Ember speaker 4 x area (W/m2 at the target); the altar 2 x spot
change.to: 6.0 W/m2 at 2700 K; altar spots 55 W with cone 30 deg, aimed to rake the cabinets from above and behind so the light passes through the acrylic

changes.expected: The cabinets read as deep translucent red with glowing edges, and the white batts show through; there is no clipping on the faces.

changes.problem: The record wall is the brightest large surface and steals the hero role from the altar.

evidence.measured: lum_median 106.2, p95 163.5 (the speaker region's median is 82-120)

change.to: 14.0 W, cone 24 deg, so the spines get scallops with dark gaps between them

changes.expected: The record wall becomes a secondary, scalloped glow; the eye travels down the room to the altar.

changes.problem: Haze puts a milky veil over the back third, so there are no true darks behind the speakers.
changes.expected: The altar zone gains depth and black; the beams of the spots stay faintly visible.

changes.problem: The shopfront glass shows no reflections and the etched name reads as an opaque beige card, so the frame does not read as taken from the kerb through glass.

evidence.measured: the 'E' panel is a uniform median 81 with hard rectangular edges and no translucency; no street reflections anywhere on the glass

change.setting: the window's etched name emission, the street lamps, and the glass finish
change.from: etched name 0.01 emission on an opaque panel; street lamps 3 x 200 W with no visible reflection
change.to: etched letters only (no backing rectangle), a frosted roughness of about 0.4 on clear glass, emission 0; let the street lamps (raise to 300 W, with one placed behind and to the side of the camera) give a soft reflection of the kerb and a lamp streak across the lower glass at about 8-12 % reflectance

changes.expected: The 'E' reads as acid-etched glass that catches the interior light at its edges, and faint reflections place the viewer outside on the street.

changes.problem: The banquette wall is washed evenly, with no pools at the tables.

evidence.measured: lum_median 98.2, p5 26.7 (the brightest wall in the room after the records)

change.setting: the Orbs and the street-lamp spill on the right wall
change.to: each Orb 4.0 W, glow 0.8, so the light sits on the table tops and the wall between the tables falls dark

changes.expected: Distinct pools on each table, with the wall between them in shadow.

changes.problem: The centre mullion sits on the vanishing point and splits the Ember pair, and the lightbox dancer is cropped to an unreadable fragment.

evidence.measured: the mullion runs x 392-408, between the speakers at x 400-425 and 478-502; only about 30 % of the dancer is in frame at x 0-60

change.to: position [-3.2, 2.2, 1.5], target [17.0, 3.4, 1.35], 32 mm, so the mullion falls on a third and clear of the altar, and the full dancer silhouette sits in the left fifth

changes.expected: The altar sits in one clear pane at the end of the room's perspective; the lightbox reads as a figure and frames the left edge.

changes.problem: The floor is a flat CG brown with no polish, wear or pendant reflections.

evidence.measured: lum_median 44.5, lum_range 68.5, r/g/b 61/41/31 with no specular streaks under the Domes

change.to: honed concrete, roughness 0.25-0.35 with a roughness map from trowel swirls and wear paths, warm grey base #5A534B

changes.expected: Soft elongated reflections of the Domes and the altar's red down the floor, giving depth and a real surface.

out_of_scope.request: Remove or desaturate the green objects near the altar so the red speakers carry the only saturated colour
out_of_scope.why: The card fixes the zone and its deep bottle-green colour; a green-red clash at the altar is a design decision for the owner

out_of_scope.request: Vary the stools and bistro tables so they do not read as one repeated model
out_of_scope.why: The seats are fixed by the room's design; only a set change approved by the owner could vary them

out_of_scope.request: Make the counter read as zinc rather than fluted timber
out_of_scope.why: The counter is fixed design; if the model shows timber where the brief says zinc, that is a model or spec question, not a picture fix

out_of_scope.request: Render at the full 2400 x 1600 to judge the denoiser smear on the record spines and the material grain at 1:1
out_of_scope.why: This proof is at scale 0.3; craft at 1:1 cannot be judged from it
